questions.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=9{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 9{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=3{x}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 9{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot 3{x}^{3}-\int 3{x}^{3}(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int 3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{x}^{3}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}9\sqrt{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(6{x}^{3/2}){|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}\frac{6{x}^{3/2}}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})(6{({e}^{2})}^{3/2})-\operatorname{ln}⁡1(6(1)^{3/2})]-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}6\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =12{e}^{3}-4{x}^{3/2}{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}} \\  & =12{e}^{3}-(4{({e}^{2})}^{3/2}-4(1)^{3/2}) \\  & =12{e}^{3}-4{e}^{3}+4 \\  & =8{e}^{3}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{3}⁡x}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{3}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})-\int (-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{3}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}}+\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{3}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}}-\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =-\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Single Logarithmic Factor
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\cdot 3{x}^{2}=\frac{3}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \,\text{d}x=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot x-\int x\cdot \frac{3}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

questions.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int {log}_{3}⁡(2x+1)\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{2}{2x+1} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{3}⁡(2x+1)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\int \frac{2x}{2x+1}\,\text{d}x]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use a substitution $2x+1=u,$ thus $2x=u-1$ and $\text{d}x=\frac{\text{d}u}{2}.$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{3}⁡(2x+1)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\int (\frac{2x}{2x+1})\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\int \frac{u-1}{u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\frac{1}{2}\int \,\text{d}u+\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{\text{d}u}{u}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\frac{u}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡u}{2}+D] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\frac{2x+1}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)}{2}+D] \\  & =\frac{2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-2x+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{(2x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-2x}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=D-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}$ is an integral constant.

$$

\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}4x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{e}u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}v{u}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot (2{x}^{2}){|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}(2{x}^{2})\cdot \frac{3}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =[2{(e)}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3})-2{(1)}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({1}^{3})]-6{\int }_{1}^{e}x\text{d}x \\  & =6{e}^{2}-6(\frac{1}{2}\,{x}^{2}){|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =6{e}^{2}-3{x}^{2}{|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =6{e}^{2}-3({e}^{2}-{1}^{2}) \\  & =3{e}^{2}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing an Arbitrary Logarithm
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{4}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x=-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{4}⁡x}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{4}⁡x(-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})-\int (-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\,{log}_{4}⁡x+\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}(-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}-\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C \\  & =-\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula $\log_4{x}=\dfrac{\ln{x}}{\ln{4}}.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Single Logarithmic Factor
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
At first, it may not look like we have two factors. Actually, we do, but one of them is implicit. The trick is to write the integral as

$$
\int \ln{x}\,\textrm{d}x = \int \ln{x} \cdot 1 \cdot \textrm{d}x.
$$

 

Using this trick, we can now use integration by parts. We let

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the by-parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x+C \\  & =x(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C.\end{aligned}
$$
